title: fix(security)!: under a wall the security catalog is the platform operator's — tenants are refused catalog writes and may only assign (ADR-0131 D3)
body:
Part of #15204

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

Stage W of #15204 (claim amendment 6112750171): the walled catalog refusal. This PR builds the refusal ADR-0131 D3 names. The C3 card's seeder and catalog-object retirement stays open on #15204 and is not part of this PR.

## The ruling this executes

ADR-0131 D3, verbatim: "Shared-DB multi-tenant (`group` / `isolated`): tenant admins cannot create or edit catalog items; the operator defines the catalog for every tenant (managed packages, Studio). Creation through Setup or the API is refused with a message naming the posture and the capability." ADR-0131 D7 adds that the catalog pages are "read-only under a wall". The server refuses whatever the UI shows. This is the refusal D3 names, not a new gate. Catalog writes stay with `manage_metadata` holders under `single` (#22621 → A, unchanged). Under a wall the authority is the platform operator's (#22801 → A).

## Measured first, on `main` at `40bc51f`

The harness was a booted `examples/app-crm` stack (`bootStack`, `multiTenant: 'posture-only'`, which gives a real non-degraded posture). It had two organizations created over `POST /auth/organization/create`. Organization A's owner was granted a set carrying `manage_metadata`, scoped to organization A. That owner is not the platform operator (`isPlatformAdmin: false`). Organization B's member held an environment set, `w_shared`, scoped to organization B.

| Door | `isolated` | `group` |
|:---|:---|:---|
| A: `PUT /meta/permission/w_shared` (adds `manage_users`) | 200 | 200 |
| B's next resolution (`resolveUserAuthzGrants`) | **gains `manage_users`** | **gains `manage_users`** |
| A: `PUT /meta/position/:name` and `PUT /meta/permission/:name` (create) | 200 | 200 |
| A: `DELETE /meta/permission/:name` | 200 | 200 |
| A: `PUT /meta/capability/:name` | 403 (`capability` is code-only) | 403 |
| A: `POST /security/_activation/permission/w_shared` | 403 (operator-only already) | 403 |
| A with CRUD on `sys_permission_set`: `POST /data/sys_permission_set` | 201, lands in the **environment ledger** | n/a |
| A with CRUD on `sys_position`: `POST /data/sys_position` | 201, an organization row with no definition | n/a |
| A: `POST /data/sys_user_permission_set` (assignment) | 201 | n/a |

**Cross-tenant write: yes.** One organization's `PUT /meta` changed what another organization's members resolve. The precondition is that a principal below the operator rung holds `manage_metadata`. A stock `organization_admin` does not hold it, and the anti-escalation deny in `default-permission-sets.ts` refuses that admin the catalog tables at the data door. The data door's edit of an existing environment set answered 404, because the wall hides the organization-less projection row. So the data door created environment sets but did not reach another organization's set.

## What changed

- **One predicate:** `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` in `@objectstack/metadata-core`, beside `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict`. Under `group` / `isolated`, a write of a `position`, `permission` or `capability` is admitted only for `isSystem` or the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` posture rung. The activation gate already reads that rung for the same reason. It is derived from the platform-admin anchors, never from a held capability. Under `single`, or with no `tenancy` service, the predicate is inert. URL spellings are folded through `canonicalMetaUrlType`, the same fold `saveMetaItem` applies, so `/meta/permissions/x` is judged as `permission`.
- **The `/meta` doors** ask it right after the capability gate. On `RestServer` that is save, reset, publish and rollback (`walledCatalogRefusal`), answering `403 FORBIDDEN`. On the runtime dispatcher it is `PUT`, answering `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. The posture is read only for a catalog type. The dispatcher reads it through `readEffectiveTenancyPosture`, factored out of the activation gate unchanged. REST reads it through the existing `resolveAnonymousFormTenancy` wiring, so the posture and the protocol come from one kernel. A tenancy service that is registered but cannot answer is a 503, never a permit.
- **The data door:** `walled-catalog-data-door.ts` (`plugin-security`), a middleware on `sys_position`, `sys_permission_set` and `sys_capability`. It runs inside the security middleware and before the permission-set write-through, so a refused write is never translated into a metadata save. Assignments (`sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set`) are not judged.
- **ADR-0087:** the semantic entry `walled-catalog-tenant-writes-retired`. The changeset carries FROM → TO.
- **Docs:** system-context census row 55b, with the counts regenerated.

### Why not `saveMetaItem`

The amendment named "the metadata door's write path, so every door that saves through `saveMetaItem` inherits it". Measured: `saveMetaItem` receives no caller principal, only an `actor` string. It cannot tell the operator rung from a tenant without a contract change on every caller. So the predicate sits where the caller is known: each door, after its capability gate. That is the activation gate's two-step shape (`refuseUngrantedActivationAuthoring`, then `refuseUngrantedActivationWrite`). It is one predicate with one sentence, and no door restates it.

## The clone door (#22881, stage CD)

CD landed first (`45e206e4`), and this PR merged it in (`d2a6934e5`). The clone door creates environment permission sets, so this PR adds the same call there:
- `permission-set-clone.ts` asks `walledCatalogWriteVerdict({ type: 'permission', ... })` right after `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict`, with the posture read through `readEffectiveTenancyPosture`.
- The call comes before any catalog read, so a refused caller learns nothing about the source or the target name. The answer is `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, the dispatcher `PUT`'s envelope.
- Pins:
  - `permission-set-clone.test.ts`: `isolated` and `group` are refused with nothing saved; the operator rung is admitted; a `single` control; the capability gate still runs first.
  - Two dogfood legs: organization A's clone answers 403 with no definition saved, and an operator control answers 200.

## Re-judged pins

- `position-write-through.test.ts`: the old walled pin was "an organization administrator's create lands its organization row, and no definition". That is the behaviour D3 refuses, so it now pins the refusal. The promotion pin seeds the pre-existing row-only position with a system write: that population is #15196 Q3 = A's.
- `builtin-positions.boot.test.ts`: under a wall, the golden's "control: create a position row" is now `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. The assignment cases do not move.

## Tests (first round at `de89dd413`; patch round 1 at code head `26c70abf8`; every later commit up to `637f1269b` is text only: docs, the changeset, the spec entry's strings, one `.describe()` string and its regenerated reference page)

- `metadata-core` 17 files / 386 tests, plus 8 new predicate cases. `plugin-security` 198 files / 4057 passed. `rest` 278 files / 5542 passed. `runtime` 355 files / 5831 passed. `spec` `src/migrations` 205 passed. Build and typecheck green for metadata-core, rest, runtime and plugin-security.
- New pins:
  - `wall-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`: `isolated` and `group`, plus a `single` control, 13 tests.
  - `walled-catalog-data-door.test.ts`: real `ObjectQL` and `SecurityPlugin`, 12 tests.
  - `meta-walled-catalog-refusal.test.ts`: the dispatcher, 11 tests.
- **Ablation, REST door:** `walledCatalogRefusal` was forced to admit, `rest` rebuilt, and the marker confirmed in `dist/` by `ablation-dist-preflight`. The 4 `/meta` dogfood pins went red, on both postures. The data-door and control pins stayed green, as expected. Restored to the `HEAD` blob and rebuilt; the marker is absent from `dist/`.
- **Ablation, data door:** the middleware registration was removed. 6 walled refusal pins went red, and the assignment, operator and `single` controls stayed green. Restored to the `HEAD` blob.
- `dispatch-gates --ran` on `5354b1601`: 125 derived, 124 run green, 1 not measured. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) because packages outside this diff are unbuilt here.
- **Ablation, clone door:** the `if (!walled.allowed)` refusal was made unreachable. The `isolated` and `group` clone refusal pins went red (2 failed, 20 passed). Restored to the `HEAD` blob.
- `permission-set-clone.test.ts` with `meta-walled-catalog-refusal.test.ts`: 33 passed. The dogfood files `wall-catalog-refusal` and `permission-set-clone-door`: 21 passed. `check:system-context-census`: OK, 129 sites (the clone door's `isSystem` read moved it from 128).
- Dogfood suite in full on the merged head: 251 files passed, 1 skipped (the report of patch round 1 on #15204, 6114447595).

## Acceptance notes

- **Not filed (no reach measured):** under a wall, an organization-scoped `manage_metadata` holder also writes the environment's objects, views and flows through `/meta`. D3 governs only the catalog. No card is filed, because only the catalog was measured.
- **Not covered here:** under a wall, ADR-0090 D12's delegated `authorEnvironmentSets` scope can no longer author environment sets at the data door. D3 refuses tenants catalog creation, and a delegate is a tenant. The delegated assignment and binding paths are untouched. `sys_position_permission_set` is not judged: under ADR-0131 D3 its rows bind nothing, and it retires with the catalog objects.
